model_annotations.Bulgarian:
**Figure 4:** This figure presents two line graphs side by side, each illustrating the sparsity ratio of SDPA (Scaled Dot-Product Attention) output values below a specified threshold, as a function of the layer index in a neural network. The left graph corresponds to a threshold of 1e-2, while the right graph corresponds to a threshold of 1e-3. Both graphs share a common x-axis labeled "Layer," which is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks and numerical labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis in both graphs is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks and numerical labels at intervals of 0.2. Each graph contains two lines: a dashed line representing the "sparsity ratio before gate" and a solid line representing the "sparsity ratio after gate." In the left graph (threshold 1e-2), the dashed line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases gradually to about 0.44 by layer 20; the solid line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.33 by layer 20. In the right graph (threshold 1e-3), the dashed line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.126 by layer 20; the solid line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.088 by layer 20. The legend for each graph is located within the plot area and includes the average sparsity ratio values for each line. The caption states that the baseline and post-gating values are similar.

**Figure 5:** This figure displays two line graphs, one on the left and one on the right, both plotting the proportion of SDPA output values below a threshold after gating, as a function of the layer index. The left graph uses a threshold of 1e-2, and the right graph uses a threshold of 1e-3. Both graphs share a common x-axis labeled "Layer," which is a linear scale ranging from 0 to 20, with tick marks and numerical labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis in both graphs is labeled "Sparsity Ratio" and uses a linear scale ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick marks and numerical labels at intervals of 0.2. Each graph contains two lines: a dashed line representing the "sparsity ratio before gate" and a solid line representing the "sparsity ratio after gate." Additionally, each graph includes a dotted line representing the "sparsity ratio after average gate," which is calculated by multiplying the average gating score with the pre-gating hidden state. In the left graph (threshold 1e-2), the dashed line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases gradually to about 0.44 by layer 20; the solid line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.33 by layer 20; the dotted line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.33 by layer 20. In the right graph (threshold 1e-3), the dashed line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.126 by layer 20; the solid line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.088 by layer 20; the dotted line starts at approximately 0.98 and decreases to about 0.088 by layer 20. The legend for each graph is located within the plot area and includes the average sparsity ratio values for each line. The caption notes that the figure also includes sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.
model_annotations.Chinese:
Figure 4 displays the mean absolute values of SDPA output before and after gating, across different layers of the model. The x-axis, labeled "Layer," ranges from 0 to 20 with linear, evenly spaced numerical ticks at intervals of 5, representing the layer index. The y-axis, labeled "Mean Absolute Value," ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 with linear, evenly spaced ticks at intervals of 0.2. The chart contains two lines: a solid gray line representing the mean absolute value before gating, which remains nearly constant at approximately 0.8 across all layers; and a dashed gray line representing the mean absolute value after gating, which also remains nearly constant at approximately 0.8 across all layers. The two lines are visually indistinguishable, indicating that the baseline and post-gating values are similar as stated in the caption.

Figure 5 presents two subplots showing the sparsity ratio of SDPA output values below a specified threshold, before and after gating, across layers. The left subplot, titled "Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-2," has an x-axis labeled "Layer" ranging from 0 to 20 with linear ticks at intervals of 5, and a y-axis labeled "Sparsity Ratio" ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 with linear ticks at intervals of 0.2. It contains three lines: a solid gray line labeled "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.03" that starts at approximately 0.03 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat; a dashed gray line labeled "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.64" that starts at approximately 0.64 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat; and a dash-dotted gray line labeled "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33" that starts at approximately 0.33 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat. The right subplot, titled "Sparsity Ratio of SDPA Output, Threshold 1e-3," shares the same x-axis and y-axis configuration. It contains three lines: a solid gray line labeled "sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.003" that starts at approximately 0.003 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat; a dashed gray line labeled "sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.126" that starts at approximately 0.126 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat; and a dash-dotted gray line labeled "sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 1.088" that starts at approximately 1.088 at layer 0 and remains nearly flat. All lines in both subplots exhibit minimal variation across layers, indicating stable sparsity ratios.
model_annotations.English: Figure 4 displays two line plots illustrating the sparsity ratio of SDPA output under different thresholds, with the x-axis representing the layer number from 0 to 20 on a linear scale, and the y-axis showing the sparsity ratio ranging from 0.0 to 1.0 on a linear scale. The left plot corresponds to a threshold of 1e-2, while the right plot corresponds to a threshold of 1e-3. In both plots, three lines are shown: a dashed gray line labeled “sparsity ratio before gate, avg 0.02” (left) or “avg 0.003” (right), a solid green line labeled “sparsity ratio after gate, avg 0.64” (left) or “avg 0.126” (right), and a dashed green line labeled “sparsity ratio after average gate, avg 0.33” (left) or “avg 0.088” (right). In the left plot, the dashed gray line starts at approximately 0.02 and remains nearly flat across layers; the solid green line starts at approximately 0.64 and remains relatively flat; the dashed green line starts at approximately 0.33 and also remains flat. In the right plot, the dashed gray line starts at approximately 0.003 and remains nearly flat; the solid green line starts at approximately 0.126 and remains relatively flat; the dashed green line starts at approximately 0.088 and remains flat. The figure caption states that the baseline and post-gating values are similar, indicating minimal change in mean absolute values before and after gating.
model_annotations.German:
Figure 4: Mean absolute values before and after gating. The baseline and post-gating values are similar.

Das Diagramm zeigt die durchschnittlichen absoluten Werte vor und nach der Anwendung von Gating über die Schichten eines Modells. Die x-Achse ist linear skaliert und verläuft von 0 bis 20, mit Tick-Beschriftungen in einem Intervall von 5, beschriftet als „Layer“. Die y-Achse ist ebenfalls linear skaliert, mit einem Wertebereich von 0 bis 1,2, beschriftet als „Mean Absolute Value“. Die Achse zeigt Tick-Markierungen in einem Intervall von 0,2. Zwei Linien sind im Diagramm dargestellt: eine gestrichelte Linie in Grau, die den Wert „before gating“ repräsentiert, mit einem durchschnittlichen Wert von 0,92, und eine durchgezogene Linie in Grau, die den Wert „after gating“ repräsentiert, mit einem durchschnittlichen Wert von 0,91. Beide Linien verlaufen nahezu horizontal und parallel über den gesamten Bereich der x-Achse, wobei die Werte leicht schwanken, aber keine signifikante Veränderung über die Schichten aufweisen. Die Linien liegen nahe beieinander, was die Ähnlichkeit der Werte vor und nach dem Gating unterstreicht.

Figure 5: Proportion of SDPA output values below threshold after gating (Left: 1e-2, Right: 1e-3). We also include sparsity measurements obtained by multiplying the average gating score with pre-gating hidden states.

Das Diagramm besteht aus zwei separaten Liniendiagrammen, die nebeneinander angeordnet sind, wobei beide die gleiche x-Achse und y-Achse verwenden. Die x-Achse ist linear skaliert, verläuft von 0 bis 20, mit Tick-Beschriftungen in einem Intervall von 5, beschriftet als „Layer“. Die y-Achse ist ebenfalls linear skaliert, mit einem Wertebereich von 0 bis 1,0, beschriftet als „Sparsity Ratio“. Die Tick-Markierungen auf der y-Achse sind in einem Intervall von 0,2 angeordnet. Beide Diagramme enthalten drei Linien: eine gestrichelte Linie in Grau, die den „sparsity ratio before gate“ darstellt; eine durchgezogene Linie in Grau, die den „sparsity ratio after gate“ darstellt; und eine punktierte Linie in Grau, die den „sparsity ratio after average gate“ darstellt. Im linken Diagramm (Schwellwert 1e-2) beginnt die gestrichelte Linie bei einem Wert von 0,98 und fällt bis zur Schicht 20 auf etwa 0,08 ab. Die durchgezogene Linie beginnt bei etwa 0,64 und sinkt bis zur Schicht 20 auf etwa 0,02 ab. Die punktierte Linie beginnt bei etwa 0,33 und bleibt bis zur Schicht 20 nahezu konstant bei diesem Wert. Im rechten Diagramm (Schwellwert 1e-3) beginnt die gestrichelte Linie bei einem Wert von 0,93 und fällt bis zur Schicht 20 auf etwa 0,05 ab. Die durchgezogene Linie beginnt bei etwa 0,126 und sinkt bis zur Schicht 20 auf etwa 0,008 ab. Die punktierte Linie beginnt bei etwa 0,088 und bleibt bis zur Schicht 20 nahezu konstant bei diesem Wert. In beiden Diagrammen verlaufen die Linien monoton fallend, wobei die durchgezogene Linie (nach Gating) stärker abfällt als die gestrichelte Linie (vor Gating), und die punktierte Linie (nach Average Gating) am flachsten verläuft.
